Curriculum Vision & Values
Curriculum Vision
The curriculum is at the heart of a school’s purpose and our curriculum reflects our core values: Endeavour, Enjoy, Excel.
At Harris Academy Tottenham we recognise that improving educational outcomes is the biggest way we can positively impact our students’ futures. We take the term ‘educational’ in its most broad sense: this means more than just a set of results. It includes a child’s intellectual development, social and emotional development, citizenship and responsibility, happiness and success.
We hope that this vision is ‘lived’ in the way teachers develop the curriculum and the way students experience it. We want a curriculum that is effectively designed and implemented, that is true to subjects’ core content and concepts, develops a love of lifelong learning, and creates beautiful work, expertise, fascination and wonder.
Curriculum principles
Our curriculum is purpose enacted. It seeks to find harmony between the four broad philosophies of what is education for: personal empowerment; cultural transmission; preparation for citizenship; and preparation for work.

Sixth Form
Welcome
Welcome to Harris Academy Tottenham. We are proud to be a double Outstanding Sixth Form, based in the heart of Tottenham.
Here you will find an innovative and academic setting for your studies, which will provide both challenge and support as you aim towards the next steps in your academic careers.
We offer outstanding opportunities with industry experts to propel you towards successful careers in your respective fields of interest. Above all, we pride ourselves in creating an environment in which you can fulfil your potential and cultivate the best version of yourself.
Applications
Applications have now closed for September 2026. If you have any queries about applications, please email the Sixth Form team on sixthform@harristottenham.org.uk.
What can you expect?
As a student at Harris Academy Tottenham, you can expect excellent tuition, small class sizes and our full support as you work towards building a successful and fulfilling future.
As part of your experience, we make sure you have the opportunity to work with, and hear from, leading practitioners in the field you are interested in. Through our partnership with Harris Federation, we deliver a programme of Master classes through which students are exposed to up-to-date research around their subject areas. Throughout the year, we ensure all students have contact with academics, practitioners, and industry experts from leading universities to facilitate academic and personal growth.
There will also be guided study support before and after school and small tutorials with specialist staff to make sure that you achieve excellently and are fully prepared for your future education and career choices.
What is your curriculum offer?
There are two strands of post-16 study available at Harris Tottenham Sixth Form. The first strand is our traditional academic curriculum. We are an academic centre of excellence that ensures our pupils gain the opportunities, support and guidance needed to access the UK’s leading universities.
The A Level courses we offer are highly regarded by Russell Group universities, specialist colleges and by top employers. Full details can be found in our Prospectus and Sixth Form Curriculum pages.
The second strand is the Kinetic Football Academy launched in 2020 to offer an individualised, innovative football and education programme for 16-18 year olds. Through our partnership with Kinetic, we are able to facilitate the aspirations of all our students, including those with a passion for football. By doing so, we secure all future outcomes for you; both academic and otherwise.
Beyond academic excellence
We see our Sixth Form students as the ultimate ambassadors for our academy; our younger students aspire to be in your shoes. As such, we place you into one of our houses, named after leading scientists and mathematicians.
Your dedicated Sixth Form tutor provides a daily point of contact for you, whilst ensuring you have the support you need to excel in your learning. There are opportunities to work alongside our younger students in a range of capacities, if you want to, so that you feel a part of our family.
Students in the Sixth Form follow a comprehensive tutorial programme which encourages them to engage with and debate challenging contemporary issues such as radicalisation, FGM, domestic abuse and the British parliamentary system. The assembly system, and programme of visiting speakers ensures that you have access to experts who provide an insight into health and wellbeing, relationships, and living in the wider world. You will also be able to take an active role within the Academy, and the Student Parliament system extends into KS5, for which elections run during the Autumn term.
Our Sixth Form continues to grow from strength to strength, and as part of the Harris Federation, we have a range of partnerships with leading universities, established through the excellent reputation of our Federation, including with the University of Oxford, King’s College and UCL.
What makes HATO6th Different?
At HATO6th, we pride ourselves on our unique approach to education. We've forged partnerships with several prestigious external agencies, bringing in mentors from internationally renowned law firms, engineering companies, football clubs, and more. Our mentoring scheme is a source of great pride for us, as it allows our students to benefit from the guidance and wisdom of seasoned professionals.
In addition to our mentoring programme, we also deliver specialist master classes. These classes not only enhance our students' learning experience but also contribute to our small class sizes, ensuring personalised attention and support.
HATO6th is not your typical sixth form institution. We prioritise academic excellence, kindness, and community in everything we do. We firmly believe in recognising the humanity and potential of every individual within our walls, and we are committed to creating an environment where students can fully realise their aspirations, and create a better world for themselves and for posterity. This dedication to nurturing the unique qualities and goals of each student sets us apart in the world of education.
Where can I find out more?
Keep an eye on the website for details of our open evening and taster afternoons, or check out our Twitter handle @HATO6thForm. Find out more about our exam results 2025.
We very much look forward to meeting you.
Ms Holly Parkinson Assistant Principal - Head of Sixth Form

Vision & Values
Our Vision and Values
Harris Academy Tottenham is a community school. We work in partnership with parents to ensure each pupil in our care has a first class educational experience, where they develop their academic scholarship alongside their character.
Our values underpin the approach we take to doing that. We instil an ethos of hard work, dedication and commitment to learning, through three core messages.
Endeavour
To ENDEAVOUR is to strive for your goals, through maintaining the highest expectations of ourselves.
Enjoy
To ENJOY is to take delight and pleasure in the learning process; To gain a feeling of success through relentless passion and drive.
Excel
To EXCEL is to achieve your full potential, through mastery of concepts and an ambition to be the best you can be.
'An unwavering belief in the potential of everyone'.
Our values are underpinned by our guiding principle. We expect colleagues to maintain the highest expectations of each and every pupil, ensuring that with support and drive, our pupils are the best they can be. We also expect pupils to believe in their own abilities.
Mantra
In our assemblies, our pupils are reminded of our Academy mantra. We share this to remind ourselves of the purpose of our learning;
"I will endeavour to do my very best, to open my mind to new ideas, and to collaborate with others to EXCEL in my own learning."

Welcome
Our belief is that children thrive when they are consistently happy and safe at Primary School. A welcome from Emily Smith, Principal: Primary.
Each child is taught in the way that suits them best and we will step in quickly if a change is needed. For some children, this might involve one-to-one support if they are finding something difficult and for others it could mean stretching them more to keep them interested.
Our Academy is relaxed and comfortable but pupils will know that good behaviour is expected of them. They will be frequently praised and rewarded for trying their best and for being kind, hard-working and well-behaved.
We want the school to feel friendly and welcoming and will always make sure that every pupil has at least one friend. Our children will be taught to respect each other and their teachers.
There is a zero tolerance approach to any type of bullying.
As they get older, pupils will have the stability of staying in the same school aged-11 – avoiding what for many children is a lost year of education as they adjust to new teachers and new surroundings.

Welcome
It is our pleasure to welcome you to Harris Academy Tottenham, confident that whatever the abilities, talents and needs of your child, we will be able to support, encourage and challenge them to reach their potential.
The decision of where to send your child to school is one of the most important that you make as a parent; thank you for investing your confidence in us.
At Harris Academy Tottenham, we have an unwavering belief in the potential of every pupil. We truly believe that every child can and will be successful, and should strive for excellence. Our Academy values embody that approach. If children endeavour to work hard, and demonstrate unwavering persistence, then they will gain enjoyment from the process of learning, and excel towards opportunities that will transform their lives.
We want our children to love coming to school; and strive to ensure that their experience here is a positive and enriching one.
An enriching experience
At our Academy, your child will develop their academic scholarship alongside their character; becoming citizens who are a credit to their local community. We provide an extensive extracurricular programme to allow your child to develop as a well-rounded person, ready and prepared to embark upon whichever pathway they desire. That is only possible through the partnership that exists between families and colleagues and partners at the academy. We are incredibly proud of the close relationships that develop between colleagues, parents, governors and pupils, and indeed they are central to all that we do.
Our curriculum is detailed and relevant, giving pupils a firm foundation in each subject discipline. Learning is fun and challenging; students have a desire to gain knowledge through dedication and commitment to their studies.
High expectations
We were delighted that OFSTED recognised this, grading us ‘Outstanding’ in all categories in June 2017. The inspectors commented that ‘learning is the business of the day’ and that sentiment underpins all that we do. Since then, the school continues to grow and strive for the highest standards. Our brand new facilities allow us to continue expanding our curriculum offer, ensuring students' experiences are both varied and enriching.
We have the highest expectations of our young people. We expect excellent presentation, good manners and respect, and a commitment to learning from every pupil.
As part of the Harris Federation – a non-for-profit charity with over 25 years experience of education in and around London, we subscribe to the notion of excellence and high expectations. Eighty one percent of all of our Academies inspected so far have been graded as Outstanding by Ofsted (compared to 21% nationally) with the rest judged as Good. Ninety five percent of our Secondary Academies have been judged as Outstanding so far. In Primary education, our Academies have been judged to be the top performing group of schools compared to all other local authorities and Academy trusts in England, in 2015, 2016 and 2017 by the highly respected Education Policy Institute.
We hope you enjoy learning a little more about us, and hope you will visit us soon.
Wayne Barnett Emily Smith Kanika Forbes

University Preparation
University Preparation - Year 12 and Year 13
Through our partnership with Harris Westminster Sixth Form, we are able to offer a unique timetable that reflects university-style learning.
Students are offered regular masterclasses and lectures from leading academics and professionals, with student-led virtual seminars hosted by the Westminster campus. This depth of learning equips students for the rigours and breadth of any university course.
Students begin their university preparations in the Autumn term of Year 12. They are introduced to universities choices, guided through the UCAS process, shown how to research courses, and prompted to think critically about their existing attainment and be strategic in boosting their predicted grades.
Medical applicants are given nuanced and extensive support through university lectures, work experience placements and volunteering in medical or carers contexts. In addition to a number of trips that we organise to a diverse range of institutions, we endeavour to show students exactly what is required to develop a genuine commitment and love of their subject.
Students receive personalised support and guidance from the Harris Federation Careers Team.
All our higher prior attaining students are also enrolled onto the Harris Experience Advanced Programme, to provide a range of opportunities that further extend learning.
This universities work complements our wider pathways and enrichment provision.

Sixth Form Curriculum
In this section you'll find out all about the courses we offer and the entry requirements.
Click HERE to download our course booklet for 2026.
All students applying to Harris Academy Tottenham must meet our general and subject-specific entry requirements. Further details of general requirements can be found on our Entry requirements page. Read our course booklet to find out about the subject-specific requirements. If there are any changes to entry requirements, these will be communicated ahead of enrolment.
Academic subjects
There are two strands of post sixteen study available at Harris Tottenham Sixth Form. The first is traditional; we’re an academic centre of excellence that ensures our pupils gain the opportunities, support and guidance needed to access the UK’s leading universities.
The A Level courses we offer are highly regarded by Russell Group universities, specialist colleges and by top employers. We expect students to complete three A-levels or equivalents in your time with us. We follow the linear pathway from Year 12. Harris Academy Tottenham does not offer opportunities to resit GCSE qualifications. For more information, please contact sixthform@harristottenham.org.uk.
Courses Offered (A Levels unless otherwise stated):
Business Studies (CTEC)
Chemistry
Computing
Economics
English Literature
Film Studies
Further Mathematics
Geography
Government and Politics
Mathematics
Psychology
Religious Studies
Sociology
Sports (CTEC)
Kinetic Football Academy
The second strand in the Sixth Form is the Kinetic Football Academy launched in 2020. Here, students typically take one CTEC qualification, alongside an A-level (receiving a total of three A-level/equivalent qualifications in total) and bespoke football coaching from leading professionals throughout the week. Students are able to select either a vocational only model, a hybrid model, or A-Level only route.
The academy adopts a holistic approach to develop each young person as a ‘whole’, rather than from just a technical or tactical component. Alongside our excellent football provision we deliver a volunteering programme, mentoring scheme, mental health support and employability workshops.
A Level and CTEC Bridging Projects
Please apply to HATO Sixth Form using the online application form. Further information, including an invitation to enrolment, will then be posted to you in the summer term.
To prepare you for your studies in Year 12 at Harris Tottenham Sixth Form, you must review and complete the relevant A Level and CTEC Bridging Projects over the summer break. Click HERE to download a document which has details of all the Bridging Projects for each subject, including links to additional resources.
Content from these bridging tasks will be used in the opening Year 12 Induction Exams in September/October - successful applicants can expect to receive more information on these exams on Enrolment day in August.
If you are still undecided as to which courses you would like to study with us, we recommend you complete the Bridging Projects to give further clarification on course content.
Don't hesitate to contact the Sixth Form Team with any further queries.

Entry Requirements
Entry Requirements
Applications for 2027-28 entry to the sixth form will open in November 2026.
Applicants applying to the Harris Sixth Form will need to attain the required entry-level standards. These are outlined below.
A minimum of seven grade 5s in full course GCSE subjects. Must obtain at least a grade 6 at GCSE in a relevant subject for the subjects being considered for A Level. Must have achieved grade 5 in English and Mathematics GCSE. A Level Mathematics requires a grade 7 at GCSE.
Must have a minimum average grade 8 from best 8 GCSE results.
3 A Level / Vocational Level 3 Combination
Minimum of three grade 5s and two grade 4s at GCSE or a merit or above in a relevant equivalent qualification (such as BTEC or CNAT Level 2). Students must choose two vocational subjects and one A level. For the A level students must have the minimum subject specific requirements. Must have achieved grade 5 in English and Mathematics GCSE.
Vocational Level 3 subjects
A minimum of five grade 4s at GCSE or equivalent, with at least a Merit or grade 4 in a relevant equivalent qualification (such as BTEC or CNAT Level 2). Must have achieved grade 5 in English and Mathematics GCSE.
Kinetic Football Academy
In addition to academic requirements, formal scholarship offer to join the football academy is subject to Kinetic Foundation staff meeting and assessing applicants to ensure they are suitable for a place on the programme; details for such sessions will be communicated once an application has been made.

Kinetic Academy Football Scholarship
Kinetic Foundation are delighted to announce a new partnership with HATO to offer an individualised, innovative football and education programme for 16-18 year olds.
As a registered charity, Kinetic Foundation adopt a holistic approach to develop each young person as a ‘whole’ rather than from just a technical or tactical component. Alongside our excellent football provision we deliver a volunteering programme, mentoring scheme, mental health support pillar and employability workshops on career planning.
Click HERE to read about HATO student Niino Adom-Malaki who has signed a two-year professional scholarship with Millwall Football Club.
Education offer
Pupils can complete a 2 A level equivalent vocational Sport course alongside 1 further CTEC or 1 A level, or a traditional 3 A level pathway. Our bespoke training and match schedule will take place outside of the timetabled lessons to ensure that pupils can undertake whichever academic pathway without any clashes.
Football offer
We employ an extensive, diverse and experienced staff body which consists of UEFA qualified coaches, strength and conditioning experts, sports therapists, youth workers, mentors, life coaches and counsellors.
Kinetic Academy scholars will train for five hours per week and play matches on a Wednesday in either the National Youth Alliance League, Bostik Youth League, FA Youth Cup or the ESFA National Cup.
Kinetic is extremely proud of their track record of supporting young people to secure professional contracts – 37 young people in six seasons have achieved this.
Next steps
If you have any further questions please contact academy@kinetic-foundation.org.uk
